The token proxy image

The token proxy is a published image, ccilabs/machine-runner-swarm-proxy on Docker Hub, not a release asset. One tag is a manifest list that covers linux/amd64, arm64, ppc64le and s390x, and Windows Server 2022 and 2025 (windows/amd64). The pipeline builds and tests it in every run, and pushes it from main only:

Event Tags pushed
A pull request or a branch None: the image is built and tested, never pushed
A merge to main sha-<12 characters of the commit>, and nothing else, by proxy-image-publish
The same merge, after the four linux-swarm jobs and every e2e group have passed edge, by the last job of the pipeline, proxy-image-edge. It stays where it is when a newer commit is on main
A release (ci/release.sh on main, the version vX.Y.Z that git-cliff computes) X.Y.Z (immutable), X.Y, X and latest, on the digest of that commit’s sha-<12> image: nothing is rebuilt

The stack files of a checkout default to latest, so the only job that changes what a checkout deploys is the release job, and it runs after every test. edge is for people who want the newest tested commit, and sha-<12> is the image of one commit that nothing has tested yet: neither is the default of anything. Before the first release latest does not exist: deploy a checkout with MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_PROXY_IMAGE set to a sha-<12> or edge tag, or use the release bundle once there is one.

X.Y.Z never moves: a release that finds X.Y.Z on another digest stops. X.Y, X and latest move only when the release is the newest of its minor line, its major line, and of all, so finishing an old release late moves nothing else. Three helper tags, sha-<12>-linux, sha-<12>-windows-ltsc2022 and sha-<12>-windows-ltsc2025, hold the parts that the jobs push first; pull the other tags.

How it is made, in the order of the pipeline (ci/proxy-image.sh, ci/Build-ProxyImage.ps1):

  1. proxy-image-linux builds proxy/Dockerfile for the four Linux platforms with buildx and QEMU, and runs each image: it reports its version, runs as 65534 with a read-only root and no capabilities, takes a token file and a state volume, and becomes healthy. proxy-image-windows-ltsc2022 and -ltsc2025 build proxy/Dockerfile.windows from the windows/amd64 binary of proxy-test on the Windows machine executors and run it the same way. ci/tests/proxy-image.sh runs the publication against a registry of its own. Windows on Arm has no machine executor, so there is no windows/arm64 image (install-windows.md).
  2. On main (the pipeline parameter publish), the publish variants of those jobs run instead, with the context scalable-machine-runner-dockerhub: they push sha-<12>-linux, sha-<12>-windows-ltsc2022 and sha-<12>-windows-ltsc2025. Then proxy-image-publish joins the three with crane index append into one manifest list, tags it sha-<12> and nothing else, checks that every platform is in it, and signs every digest keyless with the CircleCI OIDC token, as ci/release.sh signs SHA256SUMS. It records a deploy of token-proxy-image in docker-hub with the version sha-<12> (Deploys).
  3. proxy-image-edge, the last job of the pipeline, runs after proxy-image-publish, the four linux-swarm jobs and the e2e groups. It checks the signature of sha-<12> and tags it edge (not when a newer commit is on main: ci/proxy-image.sh edge). The release does not wait for it.
  4. The release job pins the digest of sha-<12> in the stack files of the bundle (MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_PROXY_IMAGE:-ccilabs/machine-runner-swarm-proxy:<version>@sha256:<digest>, in place of :latest), checks the signature, and adds the four release tags.

The credentials. The context scalable-machine-runner-dockerhub holds DOCKERHUB_USERNAME and DOCKERHUB_TOKEN (an access token that can push to the repository), and is restricted to main and to this project (Docker Hub context). Without both values a pipeline that is not the production main builds, tests, prints NOT PUSHED with the reason, and passes. On the production main (the parameter strict, set when both e2e tokens are present) a missing credential fails the image jobs, proxy-image-publish, the release and the docs publication instead: Publishing fails closed on main.

A checkout keeps the default ccilabs/machine-runner-swarm-proxy:latest, which Renovate does not manage (it is a tag with no digest). A release bundle carries its own digest, and it is the documented way to install: users download it, verify its signature and run the image that it names. Users verify the image with cosign (Verify the token proxy image); the verification must also check that the certificate names refs/heads/main (How the signature works).

Bump the runner version

The stack files pin one exact runner version by default: MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_VERSION: ${MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_VERSION:-3.1.13} in the settings of the distributor of linux/stack/runners.yaml and windows/stack/runners.yaml, and in x-env of linux/stack/microvm.yaml. It is the newest runner version that CI tests, because the tests take their runner from the same line (STACK_RUNNER_PIN in linux/tests/lib.sh, so the real-runner tests and the end-to-end jobs run the pin), and a release carries the pin that CI tested.

Each release bumps it, in a commit before the release:

  1. Pick the newest version in the manifest that has every platform (jq -r '.releases | keys[]' manifest.json, and check .releases["<version>"] for linux amd64, arm64, ppc64le, s390x and windows amd64, arm64). Read the runner changelog for the version.
  2. In the same commit, change the default of MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_VERSION in all three stack files to that version, and change the default of MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_SHA256 to the tarball SHA-256 values of that version (from the release’s checksums.txt or from the manifest: linux amd64, arm64, ppc64le, s390x in linux/stack/runners.yaml and linux/stack/microvm.yaml, windows amd64 and arm64 in windows/stack/runners.yaml, comma-separated in that order). The version must stay equal in every file. linux/tests/stack-config.sh fails when they differ, and the release job (ci/release.sh, check_runner_pin) fails when the version is not in the manifest for every platform or when a default SHA-256 list does not match the manifest for the pin.
  3. Commit it as feat(runner): pin 3.1.14 by default for a new minor or patch of the runner that users should get, or fix(runner): ... for a fix, so that git-cliff makes a release with it. Let CI run: the pin is now the version that the Swarm tests and the end-to-end jobs run.
  4. Update the version in the examples of the docs only when you want them to move (docs/operations.md uses 3.1.12 and 3.1.13 as example values).

A user then gets the new runner by deploying the new release: the pin is part of the release, and a deploy of the new stack files moves the distributor to it. A user who sets the variable keeps what they set.

The bundles come from git archive, so only tracked files ship. They leave out linux/tests/, windows/tests/, docs/ci.md, docs/releasing.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, ci/, .circleci/, proxy/ and site/: the pages about this repository’s own pipeline and release are for maintainers.

The pages that ship still link to some of those files. ci/bundle-links.py turns every relative link from a page of the bundle to a tracked file that the bundle leaves out into a link to that file on GitHub at the tag of the release (https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/blob/vX.Y.Z/...), and the release job adds the rewritten pages in place of the originals. It stops the release when a link is dead in the repository too. ci/tests/bundle-links.sh tests it on a throwaway repository and on this one, in lint-circleci, so a new page that links to docs/ci.md does not need a special case.

How the signature works

The job gets an OIDC token from CircleCI with circleci run oidc get --claims '{"aud":"sigstore"}' --root-issuer. The audience sigstore and the issuer https://oidc.circleci.com are the values that the public Sigstore certificate authority (Fulcio) accepts for CircleCI. cosign sign-blob swaps the token for a short-lived certificate, signs SHA256SUMS, and records the signature in the public Rekor log. The certificate expires within minutes, and the job keeps no key.

The certificate identity is https://circleci.com/api/v2/projects/<project-id>/pipeline-definitions/<pipeline-definition-id>. The project and the definition IDs stay the same for every branch, and a job of any branch can get an OIDC token, with no context. The identity alone therefore does not prove that main signed. What does is the source repository ref of the certificate: the extension 1.3.6.1.4.1.57264.1.14, which Fulcio fills from the vcs-ref claim of the token, so it is refs/heads/main for a release and refs/heads/<branch> for a job of any other branch. The certificate also records the repository, the workflow and the job.

cosign has flags for the GitHub extensions only, so ci/tools.sh reads the certificate itself (signed_only_on, tested by ci/tests/signature-ref.sh):

  • ci/release.sh checks the signature of SHA256SUMS with cosign verify-blob, and then that its certificate names refs/heads/main. The job stops if it does not.
  • ci/proxy-image.sh does the same for every digest of the token proxy image, right after it signs it, and again in the release job before the image gets its release tags. It reads every signature of the digest (cosign download signature), not the first one: one signature of a feature branch next to a signature of main fails the check.

To check the ref by hand, after cosign verify-blob printed Verified OK, look for the extension in the certificate of the bundle. The long hex string is the encoding of the OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.57264.1.14 followed by the value refs/heads/main, so the command matches the whole value and not a part of a longer ref:

jq -r '.verificationMaterial | (.certificate // .x509CertificateChain.certificates[0]).rawBytes' SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json | base64 -d \
 | od -An -v -tx1 | tr -d ' \n' | grep -Eq '^([0-9a-f]{2})*2b0601040183bf30010e0411(0c|13)0f726566732f68656164732f6d61696e' \
 && echo "signed for refs/heads/main" || echo "NOT signed for refs/heads/main: do not use this release"

To see which ref a certificate has, print it with openssl asn1parse: base64 -d | openssl asn1parse -inform DER | grep -A1 57264.1.14 shows the value as hex digits after HEX DUMP]:, 0C0F and then the ASCII codes of the ref.

The signing rehearsal

Signing runs for real on main only (the release job and the image jobs have the contexts), so the first merge would be its first real run, and a failure would leave sha-<12> tags with no release. The job signing-rehearsal runs the same code in every pipeline that is not documentation-only, on any branch, with no context and no secret (ci/proxy-image.sh rehearse):

  1. It starts from a registry:2 container (the second container of the job, at localhost:5000) and pushes a throwaway image: one layer with one file that names the pipeline.
  2. It gets an OIDC token with circleci run oidc get --claims '{"aud":"sigstore"}' --root-issuer, signs the image with cosign sign against the real Fulcio and Rekor (a public service: a brief failure is tried again, three times), and verifies it with verify_signature, the function that main uses: the certificate identity, the issuer, and the ref, which here is refs/heads/<the branch of the pipeline>.
  3. It checks that the same signature is refused for another ref (refs/heads/main on any other branch), so a check that has stopped looking at the ref turns the pipeline red.

Each rehearsal adds an entry to the public Rekor log with the project, the branch and the commit, like every signature of a public repository. The release requires the job. The first pipeline after a change in CircleCI’s token claims or in Sigstore shows it, and the first merge does not.

CircleCI documents that OIDC tokens are issued to jobs that use at least one context. The release job always has one, the context with GITHUB_TOKEN. In a test on 2026-10-13, circleci run oidc get also worked in a job without a context, which is why the ref and not the identity decides, and which the rehearsal relies on.

Merge method

The release notes come from the commits that land on main, so the merge method decides what the notes show.

  • Merge commit or rebase and merge. Every commit of the pull request lands on main and gets its own entry. Use this for pull requests whose commits are small, atomic Conventional Commits, as CONTRIBUTING.md asks. Entries link to their commits. The GitHub merge commit (“Merge pull request #12 …”) is not a Conventional Commit, so the notes ignore it.
  • Squash and merge. The pull request becomes one commit with the title as the message, and one entry in the notes, so write the title as a Conventional Commit. GitHub adds the pull request number, so the entry links to it. If a pull request mixes a feat and a fix, the squash hides one of them.

Mark a breaking change in a commit message, or in the title of a squashed pull request, with ! or a BREAKING CHANGE: footer.

Tag pipelines

The release creates the tag through the GitHub API, with no git push. GitHub then sends a push event for the new tag. The project uses the GitHub OAuth integration (project slug gh/CircleCI-Labs/scalable-machine-runner), not the GitHub App. An OAuth project has no trigger settings: CircleCI starts a pipeline for every push that GitHub reports, to a branch or to a tag, so the new tag starts a pipeline. In that pipeline pipeline.git.tag is the tag, and pipeline.git.branch and CIRCLE_BRANCH are empty.

That pipeline cannot release and runs no job. CircleCI does not run a job for a tag unless the job has a tag filter, and no job in .circleci/config.yml or .circleci/continue.yml has one. The setup phase also releases only when the branch is main. Look at the Pipelines page of the project after the first release: the pipeline of the new tag should show no job. To build for tags in the future, give a job a tag filter on purpose, and keep the release context out of that job.

Rerun and recovery

Rerunning is safe. Before it publishes, the job looks for a release tag at the commit that it checked out, and it never creates a second release.

Situation What to do
A test job failed Fix it and use Rerun workflow from failed. The release job runs when all jobs have passed
The release job failed before it published Rerun the job. It computes the same version
The release exists but an asset is missing, for example after an upload error Rerun the job. It finds the tag at this commit and uploads all assets again with --clobber
The job says that a tag exists at another commit Stop. Somebody created vX.Y.Z by hand, or an older release was moved. Compare git rev-parse vX.Y.Z with the commit of the pipeline. Delete the wrong tag and release with gh release delete vX.Y.Z --cleanup-tag, then rerun the job
This commit is already part of vX.Y.Z A later commit was already released. The job ended green without doing anything
The release job shows as skipped A newer pipeline is waiting for the release lock, and it will release this change too
The Deploys view shows the release as FAILED The job failed after it planned the deploy. Read the failure reason there, fix the cause, and rerun the job: it records a new deploy of the same version, and the failed one stays in the history
Nothing to release since vX.Y.Z The commits since the last release are only docs, test, ci, chore, style, refactor, or build. This is expected
gh fails with 401 or 403 The token expired or lost its permission. Replace GITHUB_TOKEN in the context and rerun the job
A release is wrong Prefer a new release that fixes it. If you delete a release and its tag, the next run makes the same version again

Rerunning a pipeline from before a later release does not release again, because the commit is already part of a tag.

Go 1.27.2 The download page of go.dev, next to the archive
cimg/base 2026.10 The digest in .circleci/continue.yml

Renovate opens a pull request for a new version and changes the version only. The pull request has the label checksum and fails on the checksum until you replace the SHA-256 value in the same branch. To update a tool by hand, change its version and its SHA-256 value together in install_tools (cosign and crane: in ci/tools.sh), and then run the steps in Try it locally. To update the image, follow Pinned versions. A Renovate pull request for the Go toolchain also moves the golang and cimg/go images, so the proxy binaries of the release use the same Go as proxy-test.

Try it locally

Everything except publishing and signing runs on a workstation. Install the tools, or run the script in the job image:

ci/release.sh install-tools # git-cliff, cosign, crane, gh into ~/.local/bin, and Go into ~/.local/go
RELEASE_SKIP_SIGN=1 ci/release.sh # the files are in /tmp/release; nothing is signed or published

To check that the release job requires every job of the workflow, as lint-circleci does, compile the config with every parameter on and read the release entry of workflows.ci.jobs:

circleci config process .circleci/continue.yml \
 --pipeline-parameters '{full-suite: true, e2e-linux: true, e2e-windows: true, release: true, publish: true}'

item.title: Contributing
item.description:
Thank you for helping to improve the machine runner swarm. This repository is part of CircleCI Labs. Field engineering reviews issues and pull requests on a best-effort basis and does not provide an SLA. CircleCI support does not cover this repository.

Reporting a bug

Search the existing issues first, and check that you use the latest release. Then open a new issue with the bug template. Include:

  • The release or commit of this repository, and the runner version. On Linux, run docker run --rm -v runners_runner-bin:/v:ro alpine cat /v/current/VERSION on the node. On Windows, run docker service logs --tail 100 runners_runner-distributor-windows.
  • The operating system of the node and the Docker Engine version.
  • The output of docker service ps --no-trunc runners_<service> and docker service logs --tail 100 runners_<service>.

Remove tokens, runner config files, and internal host names from everything you paste.

Security disclosure

Do not open a public issue for a security vulnerability. Email security@circleci.com and follow SECURITY.md.

Requesting a feature

Open an issue with the feature request template. Describe the problem you want to solve, and name the platform and the files it affects. For problems in the CircleCI platform or the runner agent, contact CircleCI support instead.

Opening a pull request

Before you open a pull request:

  1. Discuss large changes in an issue first.
  2. Run the tests for the platform you changed. Refer to Development.
  3. Update the documentation in docs/ when you change a variable, label, secret, port, or default.
  4. Write every commit message, and the pull request title, as a Conventional Commit. The release notes are generated from them, so there is no changelog entry to add. Refer to Commit messages.
  5. Check that the diff has no tokens, host names, or customer or vendor names. The repository is public.

A pull request from a fork gets no CI. The project builds no forked pull request and passes no secret to one, because the code of a fork would otherwise run with this project’s settings (Secrets and public logs). A maintainer reads the change, and to run CI on it pushes its commits to a branch of this repository by hand. Never push or mirror an outside branch to main or to a branch named smr-swarm/*: those two names get the e2e runner tokens and, on main, the publishing contexts, and the configuration of a job comes from its own branch.

A pull request that changes only documentation (docs/, site/, Markdown files) runs the lint jobs and the docs site build, and skips the builds and the Swarm tests (Documentation-only changes).

Use the pull request template. Maintainers choose the merge method for each pull request. A squash merge turns the pull request title into the commit message on main, and a merge commit or a rebase keeps your commits. Refer to Merge method.

Commit messages

Use Conventional Commits: type(scope): summary. The release job reads these messages to choose the version and to write the release notes.

Type Use for
feat A new capability, or a changed stack-file contract
fix A bug fix
docs Documentation only
test Tests only
ci The CircleCI pipeline
chore Maintenance with no user-visible change
refactor, perf Code changes that keep behavior, or improve speed

Common scopes are linux, windows, docs, readme, and ci.

A breaking change appears first in the release notes. Mark it in the commit message, in one of two ways, and write what the user has to change:

  • Add ! after the type or scope: feat(linux)!: rename the persistent service.

  • Add a BREAKING CHANGE: footer:

    feat(linux): rename the persistent service

BREAKING CHANGE: the service is now linux-persistent. Rename it in your stack file.

While the version is 0.x, a breaking change raises the minor number.

Keep each commit small and atomic.

Development

Requirements: Docker with privileged containers for the Linux suite, bash, and PowerShell 7 for the Windows unit tests.

linux/tests/run-all.sh # the whole Linux suite, a Swarm inside Docker-in-Docker
linux/tests/run-all.sh token drain # a subset
linux/tests/stack-config.sh # stack file contract, no daemon needed
pwsh -File windows/tests/Invoke-UnitTests.ps1 -InstallModules # PSScriptAnalyzer and Pester

The Linux tests run a Swarm inside docker:dind containers, so your own Docker engine never enters Swarm mode. The Windows Swarm tests run on a Windows host, and the CI pipeline runs them on Windows Server 2022 and 2025. Refer to CI/CD for the pipeline and for every lint command.

Each Linux test prints RESULT lines and exits 0 when it passes. run-all.sh runs all of them against one shared pair of Docker-in-Docker containers.

CI runs the groups as four parallel jobs, each with its own list of groups (linux-swarm in .circleci/continue.yml). A new test goes into all in run-all.sh and into one of those lists; lint-circleci fails when a group is in no list or in two. Refer to CI/CD for the lists and their durations.

Test What it checks
stack-config.sh docker stack config for every combination of stack files, the settings of each service, and the names of the Swarm configs. Needs no daemon
helper.sh setup.sh --swarm-init, --secret, and --deploy against a fresh Docker-in-Docker daemon
ephemerality.sh A new container for every job and no residue. The negative control runs docker run --restart always
exit80.sh The restart delay, no hot loop, and the exit codes 80 and 1 of the real runner
token.sh What a job can read in the default class and in the hardened class
task.sh The real runner runs tasks as the job user, against a fake API. Also the failure with CIRCLECI_RUNNER_CLEANUP_WORK_DIR=true, and a persistent runner
placement.sh Placement on a manager and a worker, and docker-build.yaml
distributor.sh The runner-distributor service: runners that wait for it and then exit 80, a node with no install, a joining node, an upgrade under three busy jobs, a rollback without a download, an exact pin that never changes by itself, 3.1, 3 and current that follow the manifest, the major-version guard, pruning to 3 versions, a tampered binary, a wrong SHA-256, and CircleCI’s real manifest. Needs network access
persistent.sh Continuous mode and persistent.yaml
microvm.sh The microVM add-on with Kata Containers: the node label, a guest kernel, DNS through the forwarder, a read-only node directory, dockerd in the VM, and the entrypoint guard. Skipped without /dev/kvm. Downloads Kata (about 1 GB) unless SWARM_TEST_KATA_DIR or SWARM_TEST_KATA_TARBALL points at a copy. Not part of run-all.sh
drain.sh SIGTERM during a job: the job finishes
limits.sh init, ulimits, pids, memory, CPU, reservations, and the capability sets take effect
network.sh Network isolation between classes, and between the replicas of a class
container-mode.sh The prototype container agent in a Swarm, against a fake API: no agent on a proxy or microVM node, a Docker-executor job with a service on localhost, the limits, no socket or token in the job, the cap, the cleanup, and the orphans. Needs the Go and pause images
bats/run.sh The unit tests of the entrypoint on cimg/base, Alpine, and UBI minimal

The suite needs no installed runner. The distributor of the shipped stack installs it, as it does for a user, from a small HTTP mirror in the harness: a manifest.json and the tarballs of the versions that a test publishes (publish_runner in lib.sh). ephemerality.sh, persistent.sh, limits.sh, network.sh, and drain.sh publish fake-runner.sh, a stand-in for circleci-runner that runs a fake job through the step-down and exits, as a single-task runner does. task.sh, token.sh, exit80.sh, placement.sh, distributor.sh, and the idle case of drain.sh publish the real runner binary, which the harness downloads once and checks against the SHA-256 of CircleCI’s manifest.

Three variables change the setup. SWARM_TEST_DIND_IMAGE sets the Docker-in-Docker image. SWARM_TEST_CACHE sets the directory that caches the real runner binary, ~/.cache/swarm-tests by default. SWARM_TEST_KEEP=1 keeps the Docker-in-Docker containers for debugging.

The Windows tests in windows/tests print CHECK <name> PASS|FAIL lines and one RESULT line, and exit 0 only when every check passes. Invoke-UnitTests.ps1 runs the Pester tests on any system with PowerShell 7. The Test-*.ps1 scripts need a Windows host with Docker in Windows-container mode, and none of them needs a runner token.

Test What it checks
Test-Injection.ps1 A stock Server Core image with the mounts of the volume runner-bin and the PATH of the stack: the toolchain, GNU tar as the task agent calls it, Git long paths, the exit codes of the runner, and the config file with environment overrides. -Online lets the real runner download its task agent. -Baked tests the baked image
Test-Ephemerality.ps1 A new container for every job and no residue, with the restart-policy negative control
Test-Exit80.ps1 Exit 80 without a hot loop
Test-Placement.ps1 Placement constraints and node labels
Test-StopHandling.ps1 What a stop does to a busy stock container (it kills the job, informational), and a Swarm secret as the runner config. -Online stops the real runner and expects a drain
Test-Install.ps1 The distributor installs the runner and portable Git from CircleCI’s real manifest into the volume of the stack, and the stock mounts work and are read-only
Test-Distributor.ps1 The distributor script against a local mirror: pin, current by SHA-256, the major-version guard, rollback, a wrong SHA-256, pruning, a changed binary, and a running container that keeps its version
Test-Persistent.ps1 Continuous mode, and a named volume that outlives the container

Swarm config names

The entrypoint and the distributor scripts reach the nodes as Swarm configs. A Swarm config cannot change, and a service keeps the old file when the name stays, so the name of each config in the stack files carries the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of its file. After you change linux/stack/circleci-runner-entrypoint, linux/stack/runner-distributor.sh, windows/runner-distributor.ps1, or a file of linux/stack/container-agent (the sources of the prototype container agent, which container-mode.yaml carries as configs), run ci/config-names.sh --write and commit the new names with the change. lint-stack, linux/tests/stack-config.sh, and the release job run ci/config-names.sh and fail on a stale name. Nobody decides when to bump a number.

Documentation checks

Documentation follows the CircleCI docs style: sentence-case headings, active voice, no contractions, and short sentences. Every docs/*.md page has front matter with page-title, page-audience, and page-description.

CI checks the relative links and the Mermaid diagrams. To run the same checks locally:

docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/input" -w /input lycheeverse/lychee:0.24.2 --config lychee.toml './**/*.md'
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/workdir" davidanson/markdownlint-cli2:v0.18.1 '**/*.md'

Pinned versions

Renovate opens a pull request every Monday for the pinned versions: the images and their digests, the tools that CI downloads, the Go toolchain and the docs theme. The configuration is renovate.json, and Pinned versions lists what it covers and what stays by hand. A pull request with the label checksum changes a version that is pinned with a SHA-256 value: Renovate cannot compute the value, so replace it in the same branch before you merge.

Pin images by tag and digest, and a new download by its version and checksum together, with a # renovate: comment above the version (see the page above). The runner version that the stack files install by default is pinned, in three places that must stay equal (linux/stack/runners.yaml, linux/stack/microvm.yaml and windows/stack/runners.yaml): the newest version that CI tests, bumped by each release (how). The alpine:3 image of the distributor is pinned by digest in linux/stack/runners.yaml. The pinned Git and 7-Zip versions and their SHA-256 values are in windows/stack/runner-distributor.ps1, and a change of the script needs ci/config-names.sh --write. Pin images by tag and digest.

Releases

Maintainers do not tag releases by hand, and nobody edits a changelog. Refer to Releasing for the details.

  • Versioning. The project follows Semantic Versioning and starts at 0.x. While the version is 0.x, a breaking change bumps the minor number. Version 1.0.0 is reserved for general availability or official adoption.
  • Release job. A CircleCI job runs on main after every test job of that pipeline has passed. git-cliff reads the Conventional Commits since the last release tag and computes the next version, with the rules in cliff.toml. A fix is a patch. A feat is a minor. A breaking change is a minor in 0.x and a major from 1.0.0. A push that holds only docs, test, ci, chore, style, or refactor commits makes no release.
  • Contents. Each release is a GitHub release with a tar.gz and a zip bundle of the user-facing files, a SHA256SUMS file, and a keyless cosign signature of that file, made with the CircleCI OIDC token. The release notes are generated from the commits, with breaking changes first. The job creates the tag through the GitHub API and never pushes a commit to main.
  • Changelog. CHANGELOG.md is a short page. The release bundle contains a generated CHANGELOG.md with every release.
  • Failures. If a release fails part way, a maintainer reruns the job in CircleCI. The job finishes the release at the same commit and never creates a second one.

Refer to Verify a release to check a download.

When the repository moves to CircleCI-Public

Replace the Labs wording in these files: the banner and the Support section of README.md, SECURITY.md, the support paragraph at the top of this file, .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml, and .github/CODEOWNERS. Decide the license, because CircleCI runner repositories use Apache-2.0 and this one uses MIT.
